stem.en: In a film, a spacecraft explodes far out in space. You see the flash and hear a loud bang at the same moment. What would really happen?

text.en: You would hear the bang a little after the flash.
You would hear no bang at all, because space has no medium to carry sound.
You would hear a fainter bang at the same moment.
You would hear the bang only if the explosion was very large.

explanation.en: Space is nearly a vacuum. Sound needs a medium to travel, so no sound from the explosion can reach you, however large it is. Light does not need a medium, so you would still see the flash.

hints.en: What does sound need in order to travel?
Is there a medium between the spacecraft and you?
